about: What the kit places pack is made from. Each piece is one model of a ready-made open kit, converted by scripts/style_packs/kit_pack.py: the archive it came in with its size and SHA-256 as fetched, the licence file read inside it, the model's path, what was left out, how it stands and how long its longest side is. A kit's archive is not in this repository; the converted pieces and kit-places.built.v1.json, the record of each conversion, are.

pack.title: Kit places
pack.description: Cozy town with a ready-made piece from an open kit where a place has a thing of its own: a rowing boat by Kenney for a fishing boat. The piece keeps its kit's colours.
pack.source_reference: Kenney, Pirate Kit 2.1 (kenney.nl/assets/pirate-kit), CC0 1.0; the piece's model is named in assets/style-packs/kits/kit-places.v1.json

pieces.reason: A fishing boat pulled up on a beach or moored at a quay is a small open boat; this is the kit's longer rowing boat, twice as long as wide, given the length of a four-metre skiff. The kit's shorter hull is left out of the pack: at 1.7 times as long as wide it reads as a tub once it stands in a place.
pieces.left_out_reason: The kit draws the oars spread, which makes the boat as wide as it is long; a boat's place is about twice as long as wide and a piece is scaled whole to fit it, so with the oars the hull would be drawn at half its length.

not_in_the_pack.fixture.well: No kit read for this pack holds a low stone well head. The roofed wells they hold are about 2.6 m tall, and a piece is scaled whole into its slot: in the 1.2 m box a drafted kind gives a well, a roofed well would stand waist high, a toy and not the thing. So the pack names no well and a well keeps the cozy town's box until a piece that is a well head exists.
not_in_the_pack.the kit's shorter rowing boat: At 1.7 times as long as wide it reads as a tub once it stands in a place.
